plugin.name: Safe (Recommended)
plugin.description:
Learned load cache. Each session records which game files and which parts of each BSA/BA2 archive Skyrim reads, from start-up until 90 seconds after your first save load. The next launch reads exactly that data back into the Windows file cache in parallel as soon as SKSE loads the plugin, so the main menu and the first save load are served from RAM instead of waiting on the disk one request at a time. The first launch only records.
Recording observes the game's own requests through SkyrimSE.exe's imports and never changes them. Saves, cosaves, writes and files outside Data are never recorded or read. Files changed since they were recorded are skipped. Prefetch size is automatic (1/8 of RAM, 512-4096 MB), stops at the RAM reserve and after 120 seconds, and is skipped on hard disks.
The log records how long the data load and each save load took. Compare a cold boot (after a restart) against Minimal to see your gain.

plugin.name: Minimal (troubleshooting)
plugin.description: Everything off: no load cache, no archive warming, no hardware probing, no process changes. The narrow SkyrimSE.exe archive flag policy stays loaded and statistics and load timings are still logged, so this is the control for comparing load times against Safe.

plugin.name: Experimental (unproven - benchmark it)
plugin.description:
The Safe load cache with a larger 6144 MB prefetch cap and 180 seconds of recorded gameplay, plus the older options testers have run on long saves: the background archive warmer (2048 MB, strided sampling), process-wide Detours file hooks, the random-access archive hint, hardware profiling and the EcoQoS opt-out.
These extras change a wider part of the process than Safe and have no measured loading advantage. Compare against Safe with the same save after a restart.
